شُوبَقٌ * A certain wooden implement of the baker, or maker of bread; (K;) a baker's rolling-pin; (MA;) [thus called, and also شُوبَك, in the present day;] an arabicized word, (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K,) from [the Pers.] جُوبَه [or Jُوبَهْ, or from the Pers. شُوبَجْ]. (TA.) [See also كَرِيبْ.]
شَبِقَ * , (S, M, O, Msb, K,) aor. شَبَقَ , (Msb, K,) inf. n. شَبَقٌ, (S, M, Mgh, O, Msb,) He was, or became, affected with vehement lust, or carnal desire: (S, M, Mgh, O, Msb, K:) said of a man; (M, Msb;) and in like manner one says of a woman; and also, sometimes, of other than human beings. (M, TA.) ― -b2- And شَبِقَ مِنَ اللَّحْمِ He suffered indigestion, or turned away with disgust, from flesh-meat. (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K.)
شَبِقٌ * Affected with vehement lust or carnal desire; (Msb, TA;) applied to a man; and sometimes to other than man: (Msb:) fem. with ة. (Msb, TA.)
